claims.text: The ARS 2026 archive dates its screwworm modeling report September 15.
claims.quote:

                           (1996-2025)
September 15
Tracking the Path of New World Screwworm
claims.scope_note: Publication date only; no model launch date is disclosed.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: The report quotes the director of the ARS livestock insects laboratory in Kerrville, Texas.
claims.text: The report quotes the director of the ARS livestock insects laboratory in Kerrville, Texas.
claims.quote:
“We now have at our disposal incredible tools to help re-eradicate New World screwworm that were not available to our predecessors, including advanced AI and predictive modeling tools that can be employed to help us forecast where New World screwworm infestations are likely to pop up,” said
Kim Lohmeyer, Director of the ARS Knipling-Bushland Livestock Insects Research Laboratory in Kerrville, TX
. “Having any kind of forewarning system that helps guide surveillance and management decisions is a game changer in our fight to respond quickly to this urgent pest.”
claims.scope_note: This locates the quoted laboratory, not the article author.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: ARS says predictive models use AI with ecological, environmental and historical information to estimate likely establishment and spread.
claims.text: ARS says predictive models use AI with ecological, environmental and historical information to estimate likely establishment and spread.
claims.quote: Predictive models use advanced analytic tools and artificial intelligence (AI) to interpret ecological, environmental, and historical information to predict where New World screwworm is likely to become established and the potential pathways it may follow to spread.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: The listed inputs include habitat suitability, temperature, precipitation and historical outbreaks.
claims.text: The listed inputs include habitat suitability, temperature, precipitation and historical outbreaks.
claims.quote:
Ecological and habitat suitability to identify landscapes and habitats that naturally support New World screwworm and map the regions in which this pest could move through favorable environments.
Environmental conditionsto monitor key factors such as temperature and precipitation, because they can directly influence New World screwworm survival, reproduction, and spread. Changes in the weather, such as seasonal changes, can raise or lower the risk of New World screwworm infestations.
Historical outbreaks and patterns to anticipate where New World screwworm may move next. The models also review past management efforts, highlighting actions that effectively slowed this pest and those that were not successful. This information will aid in the development of new mitigation strategies.
claims.scope_note: Habitat and weather are documented in the two immediately preceding source bullets.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: ARS says its models already help select areas for livestock and wildlife surveillance, adult fly trapping and sterile insect technique.
claims.text: ARS says its models already help select areas for livestock and wildlife surveillance, adult fly trapping and sterile insect technique.
claims.quote:
“ARS developed predictive New World screwworm models that incorporate historic data like habitat use, host preferences, and environmental conditions into a science-based platform that are already being utilized to select areas for increased livestock and wildlife surveillance, adult fly trapping, and for implementing SIT,” said
Lohmeyer
.
claims.scope_note: Agency operational-use account; no independent performance evaluation supplied.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: USDA uses model insights to help choose locations, timing and numbers of sterile fly releases.
claims.text: USDA uses model insights to help choose locations, timing and numbers of sterile fly releases.
claims.quote: USDA uses insights from the models to identify optimal locations, timing, and the number of sterile flies to release for the most effective application, to interrupt their reproductive cycle and spread.
claims.scope_note: Do not draw an actual forecast or measured target without underlying data.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: Sterile insect technique releases sterilized male flies to mate with females in the wild population.
claims.text: Sterile insect technique releases sterilized male flies to mate with females in the wild population.
claims.quote: Eradication of NWS infestations is accomplished through the sterile insect technique. Sterilized male flies are released to mate in an area with an established NWS population. Females, only mating once in their lifetime, then lay nonviable eggs. The population decreases without the addition of new larvae and dies off naturally over a few lifecycles.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: After mating with sterile males, females lay nonviable eggs that cannot hatch.
claims.text: After mating with sterile males, females lay nonviable eggs that cannot hatch.
claims.quote: Sterilized male flies are released to mate in an area with an established NWS population. Females, only mating once in their lifetime, then lay nonviable eggs.
claims.scope_note: An illustration of the biological mechanism does not establish eradication in a particular place.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: ARS warns that the models cannot predict every scenario, particularly transport of infested animals by people.
claims.text: ARS warns that the models cannot predict every scenario, particularly transport of infested animals by people.
claims.quote: “However, these models cannot predict every scenario, especially those impacted by unpredictable variables like people transporting infested animals.”
claims.scope_note: A limitation on prediction, not proof transport is wholly excluded from every model.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: TAHC tells owners to monitor animals closely.
claims.text: TAHC tells owners to monitor animals closely.
claims.quote:
Look at your animals closely and often. Diligent monitoring of animals is key to preventing infestation and avoiding large impacts.
Check livestock and companion animals for evidence of NWS infestations, including flies, maggots, larvae, or eggs.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: TAHC directs immediate reporting of suspected and confirmed screwworm cases.
claims.text: TAHC directs immediate reporting of suspected and confirmed screwworm cases.
claims.quote: Early detection and reporting is critical. Report all suspected and confirmed cases of NWS immediately.
claims.scope_note: Source reporting section specifies immediate reporting; full wording is preserved in the fetched snapshot.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

claims.statement: USDA tells livestock owners never to move an animal showing signs of infestation or suspected of being infested.
claims.text: USDA tells livestock owners never to move an animal showing signs of infestation or suspected of being infested.
claims.quote: Livestock owners should remain vigilant and never move an animal that exhibits signs of infestation or that is suspected of being infested. Livestock owners should work with their state animal health officials and ensure they are following all requirements before moving any livestock or wildlife in and out of infested areas.
claims.evidence_scope: Full supporting sentence or passage, retained for internal factual verification.

rejected.claim: The hard part is where to release them.
rejected.reason: The supplied narration ranks this as the hardest challenge; no source makes that comparative assessment. Replace with a neutral location question.

rejected.claim: A new USDA report from Kerrville.
rejected.reason: The source locates the quoted lab director in Kerrville; it does not establish where the report was authored. Attribute the statement to that lab director.

rejected.claim: The model has a blind spot: people can transport infested animals.
rejected.reason: The research draft makes the limitation categorical. ARS says not every scenario is predictable, especially transport, rather than claiming every model excludes it.

rejected.claim: A rancher can move animals when the defined quarantine restrictions are lifted.
rejected.reason: This candidate consequence requires all remaining movement conditions and exact zone geography. It is excluded from this short film; no zone-release claim is accepted here.
